payload.markdown: Predictability is an important aspect of object-oriented programming. You should design your classes so that users of objects can be sure of their features. One way you can make an object safe is to render predictable the types of data it holds in its properties. One might ensure that a $name property is always made up of character data, for example. But how can you achieve this if property data is passed in from outside the class? In the next section, I examine a mechanism you can use to enforce object types in method declarations.

items: Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Constructor: __construct initialises each new object; promoted parameters collapse the boilerplate.
Constructor Property Promotion: Declaring constructor parameters as properties in a single step (PHP 8).
Properties & Methods: Class state held in properties, and behaviour implemented as methods.
References: Two variables sharing one value slot, created with =&.
Visibility & Encapsulation: public, protected and private control who may read or write a member.
Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
Data Mapper: A layer that moves objects to and from storage without the object knowing SQL.
